spans.s:
kṣarapuruṣa
(‘the being who changes’)
------------------------------------------
In the Bhagavadgītā (15.16) Lord Śrī कृष्ण describes two kinds of puruṣas or beings: the क्षर and the अक्षर.
All the living beings and objects associated with प्रकृति or nature—whether it is ब्रह्मा the creator or the blade of grass—are ‘kṣara’ puruṣas since they are subject to change. The ‘akṣara’ puruṣas are the liberated souls, ever established in their essential changeless nature.
Sometimes ‘kṣarapuruṣa’ is interpreted as the products of प्रकृति (mother nature) and ‘akṣarapuruṣa’ as the māyā-power of God.

kṣattriya
(‘one who protects others from injuries’)
------------------------------------------
See VARṆA and VARṆĀŚRAMA DHARMA.

kṣara
(‘destructible’)
------------------------------------------
Literally, the word क्षर stands for anything that gets destroyed, that is ephemeral.
However, the Bhagavadgītā (15.16) uses it in a technical sense. According to it there are two kinds of beings—the kṣarapuruṣas and the akṣarapuruṣas.
All beings associated with प्रकृति (i.e., embodied beings undergoing transmigration)—starting with the fourfaced ब्रह्मा right up to a blade of grass—are ‘kṣara’ whereas the muktapuruṣas or liberated souls, are ‘akṣara’ since they are not associated with the everchanging प्रकृति.
